thread.title: Apple: The World Is Not Ending - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) | Seeking Alpha

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple: The World Is Not Ending - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) | Seeking Alpha
text:
On Monday, shares of technology giant Apple ( AAPL ) fell by nearly 4%, leading the tech sector and overall market lower, after another report came out about iPhone production cuts. If it seems like this kind of news comes out almost daily, well, you might be right. We've heard concerns from all over the supply chain, leading to many negative pieces surrounding the name. Fortunately, for investors, Apple's world is not ending anytime soon.
If you didn't see my Apple article last week discussing this subject, I encourage you to do so. This is not the same company that lost a third of its value a few years ago when the iPhone 6S line did not pan out as hoped. More expensive products these days can soften the blow from unit sales, and Apple is generating more recurring service revenues than ever before. In fact, services numbers will be even higher moving forward as Apple has made an accounting change related to how products/services are reported.
Sure, guidance at Apple's most recent earnings report wasn't great, and a number of suppliers have issued some downbeat comments. A chunk of this is due to the trade war, which if the US/China ever come to an agreement, would likely send Apple and the overall market higher. Don't forget that Apple still hasn't made major headway in India , a market that could open up huge sales potential in the future. Finally, don't forget that reported results are being impacted by foreign exchange rates, so a meaningful pullback in the dollar would likely create a major tailwind for Apple and many US multinationals.
If Apple was at all concerned about revenue growth, there are many levers the company could pull. Another version of the iPhone SE at a $349 or a lower price point could sell millions of units a year. Perhaps, if the company wanted to get its PC market share significantly into the double digits, it could launch a drummed-down MacBook for $799 or less. If management wanted to disrupt the tablet market, what about an iPad mini that starts at $249 or perhaps even $199? With DRAM prices dropping, some of this might be possible. Just imagine the improvements that can be made over the iPad mini 4 below by removing the Home button as we've seen in the new iPhones and iPad Pros.
( Source: MacRumors iPad mini page, seen here )
Apple has dominated the premium space for its products, but a simple move down the price ladder a little could mean tens of billions in extra revenues a year. The above-mentioned items are just a few extras that I've speculated about, beyond things expected in 2019 like updated AirPods , the Apple TV service , and perhaps a second generation of HomePod . Apple's charging mat may even make an appearance at some point. Of course, there also are major opportunities down the line if Apple launches smart glasses or were to ever enter the vehicle business.
As I mentioned in my previous article, even with all of this bearishness, Apple is still likely to see overall revenues rise in the low to mid-single digits. That's the opposite of what happened in 2015-2016 when analysts were calling for high single-digit percentage declines in the top line. Earnings per share will likely rise at an even faster rate moving forward, primarily thanks to the buyback. That means you are paying less than 14 times current year earnings for this stock, a very reasonable valuation. Just take a look at the graphic below to see how much the company has returned to shareholders in recent years, and yet there still is a net cash position of more than $120 billion. The recent drop in the stock means the buyback is even more powerful, and investors buying now receive a higher dividend yield.
( Source: Apple capital return plan page, seen here )
While the news media may make it seem like the world is coming to an end for Apple, that's obviously not the case. While there might be a little short-term weakness if the expensive iPhones don't sell well , the company has several demand levers it can pull if it's interested purely in revenue growth. There will be many new products and services coming in future years, and the name still boasts the best capital return plan on the street. Remember, this isn't the same company that dropped more than 30% a couple of years ago, and those who bought that panic have done quite well since.
